Runic forging Craft notable +5% chance for a runic action to cost half the potential
5% reduced potential cost of runic actions
Inscription Gate: You can build the Inscription Gate, a Runecarver portal with pink-violet runes. Shift + use on it opens the map of every portal in the world: pick one and inscribe the link, and everyone who enters the gate steps out there.
Azurite Sight: Azurite veins within your view radius are marked on the map and minimap: plain, corrupted and divine each with its own icon. A vein mined out by more than three quarters is no longer marked.
Divine Touch: +2% chance for divine azurite; Each chisel hit on a plain azurite vein outside the mist has a chance to turn it divine, with the same lightning as a heavenly strike. Any chisel works, in any biome.
Ascendant Rune: +10% chance that a property added by a rune rises one tier; When a rune adds or raises a property, it has a chance to rise one tier more as a separate step, beyond the item's level limit. You see a second flash, hear a chime and read "+1 affix tier".
Perfect Inscription: +10% chance that a property rolled by a rune takes the highest value of its tier; A property rolled by a rune (Fate included) has a chance to take the highest value of its tier.
Portal Crate: Away from a workbench, dismantling a portal packs it into a crate that keeps its tag, author, durability and Inscription Gate link. Place it back from the crate anywhere. A crate cannot pass through a portal.
Relic Passage: Dragon eggs for summoning, Hildir's chests and dvergr parts (charred cogwheels, dvergr needles, mechanical springs) go through portals, with no portal toll. Ore and metal are not included.
Vacuum Chest: Unlocks the Vacuum Chest at the Rune Carver Table. It takes finished goods from smelters, kilns, spinning wheels and windmills around it and feeds them from its contents. Shift + mouse wheel sets the radius, Shift + E the kind of goods it collects.
Chisel Quarrying: Rune chisels also mine stone and ore deposits, like a pickaxe of the same metal: bronze, iron or black metal (flametal hits as hard as black metal). A deposit too hard for that pickaxe is too hard for the chisel. Chisel hits do not train the Pickaxes skill. Azurite veins are mined as before.
Last Touch: Runic crafting can overspend an item's potential while any potential remains; the rest drops to zero.
Runic Vise: +1 capacity when crafting with runes; One more alloy or glyph slot at the Runic Anvil, on top of the anvil's own slots.
Spared offering ×6 Craft node +2% chance to spend nothing boss fragment
Treasure maps from chests ×3 Craft node +2% chance of an extra treasure map from chests
Treasure maps from kills ×3 Craft node +2% chance of an extra treasure map from kills
Unusual ore ×3 Craft node +2% chance for extra unusual ore
Unusual ore Craft notable +5% chance for extra unusual ore
Clean Split: A seam your pickaxe beats by two tiers shatters in one blow
Ore Portals: Ore and metal bars pass through portals once the boss of their biome is dead; the portal keeps a share of what passes (25%).; • Copper, tin, bronze — The Elder; • Iron — Bonemass; • Silver — Moder; • Black metal — Yagluth; • Flametal — Fader
Ore Sight: Ore deposits within your view radius are marked on the map and minimap; the marks clear as soon as they leave that radius
Hidden Vein: 5% chance that a hit on stone knocks out a random ore of a biome whose boss has been defeated on the server; 5% chance that Mining stone knocks out a random ore from a biome whose boss you have defeated
Cascade: A shattered deposit has a 5% chance to shatter a random deposit nearby; each such shatter rolls again; Shattering a deposit has a 5% chance to Shatter a random deposit nearby. The chance cascades: each deposit it Shatters rolls again, so with enough luck a whole mine bursts in a chain
Smelted Lode: 5% chance that ore drops already smelted, as its bar; 5% chance that ore drops already smelted, as its bar
Precise Strike: Every hit into a weak spot also yields an extra share of the deposit’s ore.
Focused Seam: Weak spots of the mining mini-game appear only on the deposit being mined

Keywords¶

Changed (20)¶

Name Change
Ailment An effect applied by matching damage. Most → Burning ailments → and use → shock roll against layers built by recent hits, bleeding and poison have a chance per hit, chill fills an ailment gauge; impale uses stacks, while armour break and stagger have their own accumulation rules.
Ailment gauge Matching → Chill damage → and fills → armour break fill the target's ailment gauge, and so do bleeding and poison from ground effects; reaching the gauge threshold applies the ailment. Further hits sustain it, while a pause lets the gauge drain and ends the ailment when empty.
Ascension A boss → Lord's essence → Brand ascends a → any weapon, → piece shield → of or summoning staff → equipment to the biome after its boss. Base → Weapons, shields, armour and summoning staves: base damage (in the item's own damage types), durability, block and block → armour rise to that biome's weapons → items of the same kind and slot - nothing goes down; a summoning staff's minion becomes as strong as that biome's creatures. Workbench → Their workbench upgrades start over at quality 1 and then cost what that biome's weapon → reference item costs. Properties, sockets, sigils and implicits stay. One → Equipment essence → with per → nothing item → to compare - rings, and → belts, amulets, trinkets, utility items, capes without armour, tools - gains only upward. Rings and belts can also ascend: only their item level rises, unlocking higher property tiers on future rolls. → ; Their current → its properties, implicit effects, base stats, durability and quality remain unchanged. One brand per item, and only upward.
Bleeding Slash damage fills → can the → inflict bleeding gauge → by chance; there is no base chance. When it fills, bleeding → Bleeding deals 20% of the slash damage of the strongest hit in → that the → inflicted build-up → it per second for 4 s, over time and through armour. Bleeding damage, the damage over time multiplier and duration change it separately. Each player keeps their own strongest bleed on a target; a → an weaker → equal or stronger one does not refresh → refreshes it.
Build-up Makes matching damage apply an ailment more readily. It → For does → burning not → and add → shock it enlarges each layer a missing → hit damage → leaves; type → for bleeding and poison it increases their chance, increase → and ailment → its damage → flat or → form extend → is duration; → a flat chance. Chill and armour break still fill a gauge, impale uses an application chance instead of a gauge.
Burning Fire damage fills the burning gauge. When it fills, burning deals 25% of the fire damage of the strongest hit in the build-up per second for 4 s, as fire damage over time. Burning damage and the damage over time multiplier make it stronger, duration makes it last longer. Each player keeps their own strongest burn on a target; a weaker one does not refresh it. Wet shortens it, and chill removes it.
Every fire hit leaves a layer of flammability on the target for 8 s, the larger the more of the target's ailment threshold it dealt; the layers add up to 100%, and each hit ignites with a chance equal to them. Burning deals 25% of the fire damage of the igniting hit per second for 4 s, over time; each player keeps their own strongest burn on a target. Tar makes a target more flammable, wet less and shortens burning; chill stops its damage while it lasts, and its time keeps running.
Careful Builder Your attacks cannot damage player-built pieces, including your own. Enemy attacks and natural objects are unaffected. You can still dismantle pieces with the hammer. Carts, ships and siege machines, which the hammer cannot dismantle, can still be broken.
Charged attack A charge empowers your next released weapon attack and is consumed even on a miss. Charges do not stack or expire. A charge source can charge the attack again only after its cooldown: 2 s, a critical hit 0.2 → 1.2 s, counted from the last successful charge. A perfect dodge ignores the cooldown and always charges the attack if a dodge roll charges it for you. Spending a charge does not restart cooldowns, and failed grants do not extend them. All hits and projectiles of the released attack share its charge. Spells can consume it only with Charged Casts. The charge itself grants 25% increased damage; charged-attack nodes add further bonuses.
Chill Frost damage fills the chill gauge. Chill slows movement, weakens over time and removes → stops the damage of burning while it lasts; frost-resistant creatures are protected from the slow.
Effective Range Bow and crossbow shots deal full damage up to their effective range. Beyond it, damage first decreases gradually, then falls more steeply to a fifth at the far limit. Increased effective range stretches the entire curve. Crossbows have no effective range: they deal full damage at any distance.
Fire and Frost Burning and chill cannot → live coexist → together. Applying → While either → a removes → target is chilled its burning deals no damage, but the other → burning's time keeps running; once the chill ends, the burning hurts as usual.
Fire damage An elemental damage type that → whose fills → hits build flammability on the target and can ignite it (burning gauge → ). Damage from the hit is separate from burning damage over time.
Life leech Restores a share of health actually removed by a qualifying hit after armour and resistances. Weapon and projectile hits use life leech; spell hits use spell leech, while indirect damage and resource hits do not qualify. Each hit starts its own leech that restores 2% of maximum health per second until it has given back its share; all leech together restores at most 20% per second and stops at full health.
Restores a share of health actually removed by a qualifying hit after armour and resistances. Weapon and projectile hits leech only from their physical damage (blunt, slashing, piercing) - the fire, frost, lightning, poison and spirit of an attack restore nothing; spell hits leech from all their damage through spell leech, while indirect damage and resource hits do not qualify.
Lightning damage An elemental damage type that → whose fills → hits build conductivity on the target and can shock gauge → it. A shocked target takes more damage and builds up stagger faster for a few seconds.
Phantom Strikes A melee attack hit can cause a phantom strike against a random nearby enemy, including the original target. Only the weapon's own blow counts: projectiles, spells and area blows such as a sceptre's Smite lightning do not. It deals 24% of the original hit's calculated damage before the target's defences. Damage modifiers are not applied again, and it does not roll a new critical strike or trigger on-hit effects. It rolls its own critical strike with the critical strike chance and damage of the original hit plus those for phantom strikes. It builds up no ailments, and it builds up half the stagger of the original hit, raised by stagger build-up for phantom strikes. Every full 100% chance guarantees one phantom strike; the remainder rolls for one more. Only Endless Apparition allows phantom strikes to trigger further phantom strikes.
Poison Poison damage fills the → can poison gauge → by chance; there is no base chance, and every full 100% of chance adds a certain poison. When it fills, → Each poison deals 15% of the poison damage of the strongest → its hit in the build-up per second for 4 s. Each → on its own timer; a player can keep → keeps up to 3 poisons on a target at once, and a → the poison limit raises that; → , and a new poison on a full set → one replaces the weakest, if it is stronger. Poison damage and the damage over time multiplier make it stronger. Poison is separate from elemental damage.
Poison damage A damage type that fills the → can poison gauge → by chance. It is separate from elemental damage and from poison damage over time.
Rarity Items: Common items have no random affixes. Magic items have 1–2 affixes: at most 1 prefix and 1 suffix. Rare items have 3–4 → 6 affixes: at most 2 → 3 prefixes and 2 → 3 suffixes. Implicit properties do not count towards these limits. Unique and Legendary items have their own properties and rules. Creatures: no stars means Common, 1–2 stars Magic, 3–4 Rare, and 5 or more Unique. Each star grants a modifier and increases health, damage and loot.
Shock Lightning damage fills the shock gauge. When it fills, the target is shocked for 3 s: it takes more damage from every source and builds up stagger faster, both by the shock's strength. Strength depends on the lightning damage of the strongest hit in the build-up, before the target's defences, compared with the target's ailment threshold: a hit of 1% of it shocks for about 8%. Below 5% there is no shock, and it never goes above 50%. Shock effect makes it stronger, ailment duration makes it last longer. Only the strongest shock on a target acts, and a weaker one does not refresh it. Shock is not a stun and deals no damage itself.
Every lightning hit leaves a layer of conductivity on the target for 8 s, and each hit shocks with a chance equal to all layers, up to 100%. A shocked target takes 20% more damage from every source and builds up stagger faster for 3 s; shock effect raises this, up to 50%. Only the strongest shock on a target acts, and it deals no damage itself.
Slash damage A physical damage type that fills → can the → inflict bleeding gauge → by chance. Bleeding requires → needs both slash damage, not just → and a build-up → bleeding bonus → chance; there is no base chance.

New (9)¶

Name Change
Ammunition Bombs or any thrown ammunition, including thrown meads
Ballista A crossbow construct, set up with the siege hammer by any character. It is a skill, not a building: it costs nothing and can stand anywhere, bound only by the ballista limit. It carries a copy of the crossbow in the siege crossbow cell and shoots real bolts from the bolt magazine. When set up it records the crossbow's own damage and a share of its builder's crossbow, projectile, reload and fire-rate bonuses; changing gear later does not change it. Its durability is its crossbow's and runs out by itself in its lifetime, 12 seconds at base; every shot wears it a little more, at zero it falls, and the hammer repairs it. It shoots only while its builder is near.
Construct A construct is an object a character sets up or creates that acts on its own: ballistas, ice crystals, spores, armour shards, Mountain Bells, and a Steelskaldr's living weapons. Its durability is its health, and it runs out by itself in its lifetime: effect duration lengthens the lifetime and reduced decay slows the loss. At zero a ballista falls and the created ones go off. Living weapons do not decay: their durability is a real item's. A bonus for constructs reaches every construct that has the bonused property.
Damage over Time Speed A damaging ailment deals its damage faster: burning, poison or bleeding with 25% increased damage over time speed deals 25% more damage per second and ends sooner, so its total damage stays the same. General rows and rows of the ailment add together.
Mountain Bell Tags: skill, construct, area, damage, build-up.
Hold your alternative attack to see the place and the eitr it will reserve, release to call the Bell: it falls from the sky on the ground in front of you, up to 14 m away, and its landing hurts nobody. A bad spot or too little eitr refuses the call and costs nothing.
Cooldown 8 s, the same for every sceptre of this character. It stands 20 s (base 20), its wave reaches 4 m (base 4), you keep up to 1: a new Bell at the limit replaces your oldest. Each Bell reserves 35% of maximum eitr until it leaves, you die or the sceptre comes off.
Every weapon hit on it, yours or an ally's, shots included, rings it: a wave passes 40-60% of that hit to each enemy around, damage and every build-up alike. Crit, leech and kills belong to the one who struck; defence, resistances and conditions are the enemy's own. Enemy hits, damage over time and other waves do not ring it. Striking it is not hitting an enemy: the blow itself gives no on-hit reward.
Scales with: area of effect (it grows the area, so the radius grows as its square root), effect duration, construct and Bell rows, eitr reservation efficiency; the wave with the damage, build-up and area damage of the one who struck.
Phantom socket A socket beyond the item's socket limit, opened by the Glyph of the Void. It takes what an ordinary socket takes and stays through punches, reforging and repairs.
Potential An item's budget for runic crafting: 100 on every ordinary piece of equipment. Each runic action costs 15 plus the costs of its alloys and glyphs; a critical craft costs half. At zero the item still works, but runic crafting is closed. Repairs and workbench upgrades do not restore it.
Runic Anvil A crafting station for alloys and glyphs. Its stock keeps one slot per kind with no limit; upgrades open up to four shared slots, and a Runecarver adds one more of their own. Forging makes the item rare with two prefixes and two suffixes; alloys make the properties of their theme more likely.
Unusual ore Each unit of ordinary copper, tin, scrap, silver or flametal mined may come with one unusual ore of the same metal beside it, at a small chance. The unusual ore smelts into a themed alloy for the Runic Anvil.
